THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 24.09.2019, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C).No.13989 OF 2019(W) 2  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has approached this Court seeking that demolition of his building, as was ordered by the Municipality through Ext.P2, be completed forthwith, since 60% of it has already been demolished and continuation of the balance causes irreparable prejudice and damage to him,
particularly because mutation of the property, which houses this building and purchased by him from an earlier owner, has not been effected in his name solely on account of the illegal construction which is now sought to be demolished.

2. The petitioner alleges that demolition has been now stopped by the Municipality singularly on account of the objections raised by the 3rd respondent, who is a tenant of another building, which is not covered by Ext.P2 and who will not be in any manner prejudiced by the demolition.

The petitioner adds that the 3rd respondent had, in fact, approached this Court earlier by filing W.P(C)No.35211 of 2015, which was dismissed finding him to have no locus standi and that this judgment had been confirmed by a Division Bench of this Court in W.A.No.1023 of 2019.
The petitioner, therefore, prays that Ext.P2 be now directed to be implemented fully.

3. The learned Senior Counsel- Smt.Sumathy Dandapani, instructed by Shri.Millu Dandapani,
appearing on behalf of the petitioner, adds to the afore narration, by saying that the 3rd respondent,
having been found without any locus standi to challenge the demolition of the building covered by Ext.P2, is now attempting various other methods to ensure that such action is delayed.

She says that there is no reason for the Municipality to accede to such attempt, especially the 3rd respondent will not be, in any manner, affected by the demolition because he is occupying another building, which is unconnected with the building sought to be demolished.

The learned Senior Counsel, therefore,
prays that Ext.P2 be directed to be implemented fully without any further delay.

4. The learned Standing Counsel- Shri.V.Ranjith Kumar, appearing for the Varkala Municipality,
submits that his client has no objection in implementing Ext.P2 but that they were constrained to stop the work, after demolition of nearly 60% of the building, on account of the objections raised by the 3rd respondent and also in deference to the on going litigations.

He, however, confirms that the cases at the instance of the 3rd respondent have been dismissed by this Court and therefore, that as matters now stand, there is no legal impediment for implementation of Ext.P2 any further.
He says that the Municipality is, therefore, willing to continue with the demolition work, affirming that the 3rd respondent will not be prejudiced in any manner.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent-Sri.K.Mohanakannan, submitted that his client's anxiety was only that on account of the demolition of the alleged illegal portions of the building in question, he should not be forcibly evicted therefrom, particularly because he has already approached the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions seeking orders against the Municipality for licence to run his hotel business in the said building.

He says that his client has no other objection against the demolition but that, as is clear from Ext.R3(h), the Tahsildar, Varkala,

2 has, in fact, ordered the petitioner herein to reconstruct the demolished building.

sentences.text: 6. I have considered the afore submissions and have also examined the materials and pleadings on record.

7. There is no doubt that the Municipality has issued Ext.P2, ordering demolition of the building in question and that 60% of the same has been completed, which fact is also conceded to by the other parties.

The only question, therefore, is whether demolition of rest of the building should be held up on account of the objections raised by the 3rd respondent or solely on account of certain proceedings that are stated to have been taken by the Tahsildar, as is submitted by the 3rd respondent, relying on Ext.R3(h).
8.

Pertinently, the 3rd respondent does not have a case that he is conducting any business or that he is in possession of the offending structure; and it is submitted before me by both the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the Municipality that his business is being conducted in a completely different building.

I, therefore, fail to understand why the 3rd respondent should object to demolition of the building in question as per Ext.P2,
particularly when he has been unable to obtain orders from this Court through successive litigations.

9. Coming to Ext.R3(a) proceedings, which is stated to be at the instance of the Tahsildar, I fail to understand how the 3rd respondent can take refuge under it either, since nothing has been placed before me to show the validity of such proceedings or as to how it was issued.

10. I am, therefore, of the firm view that Ext.P2 must be implemented de hors any other proceedings, unless the parties are able to obtain necessary orders from a competent Court or Authority against it.

Since there is no such proceedings available on the files of the case as of now, I do not deem it necessary to keep this writ petition pending any further and therefore, deem it appropriate to dispose it of in the following terms

For the reasons above, I order this writ petition and direct the Secretary of the Varkala Municipality, namely the 2nd respondent herein, to immediately commence work to demolish the offending structure, as mentioned in Ext.P2, in terms of law, and to complete the same as expeditiously as is possible, but not later than three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

If, for any reason, the building in possession of the 3rd respondent is also sought to be proceeded against under the directions in Ext.P2, he shall be properly notified and offered an opportunity to make his objections; reiteratingly clarifying that if his building is not in any manner involved, then no such opportunity requires to be given and that demolition can be taken forward in terms of law,
as directed afore.
Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN JUDGE MC/24.9.19 APPENDIX PETITIONER'S/S EXHIBITS:
